narrative:
The model estimates a 69% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your professional profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest element pushing the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, only about half have similarly limited experience, while many others bring 6 or more years; the model sees shorter tenure as a common reason people move on.

The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most important factor and pulled the prediction even more strongly toward leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay do not report receiving outside opportunities, so this availability of alternatives signals higher risk of departure.

Your employment in the “other” sector, rather than medical or education fields, was the third notable influence and also nudged the outcome toward leaving. This sector shows a somewhat higher turnover pattern in the data.

Although several positive aspects appear in your profile—such as feeling recognized, having job stability, and reporting high emotional commitment—the model weighed your limited experience and external opportunities more heavily. 

The organization should consider discussing retention options with you, such as accelerated career development or clearer promotion paths. You may wish to reflect on whether the external opportunities better match your goals.
